Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
826 PM EDT Tue Sep 1 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Sever Thunderstorm Watch through midnight for Harford and Cecil
counties in northeast Maryland.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Daily severe weather threat through the end of the week.

- 2) Hot and humid conditions yield possible record high 
 minimum temperatures this week

- 3) Decreasing heat & thunderstorm chances heading into Labor 
 Day weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Daily severe weather threat through the end of 
the week.

Aloft, upper level ridging over the Ohio River Valley slowly
shifts eastward this afternoon as a shortwave trough pivots
over the forecast area. At the surface, a strong low pressure
system tracks east across Canada through the end of the week
with the associated fronts lingering near the forecast area. On
Friday, the associated cold front tracks across the forecast
area. Daily shower and thunderstorm chances continue through 
the end of the week across the forecast area with a hot and
humid airmass yielding ample CAPE (1500-2500 J/kg)each
afternoon.  

The forecast for Wednesday through Friday remains uncertain 
regarding timing and thunderstorm coverage. Should thunderstorm 
development coincide with peak daytime heating, instability will
yield strong to severe thunderstorms across the forecast area. 
The best chance for severe weather is on Thursday as the 
aforementioned cold front approaches the forecast area. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Hot and humid conditions yield possible record high 
 minimum temperatures this week

A hot and humid airmass builds overhead this week with heat
indices soaring into the upper 90s to low 100s each afternoon.
Uncertainty with max heat index tomorrow due to potential
convection and cloudcover. May end up with some advisories. 
However, Thursday has the potential to be the warmest day of the
week with heat indices forecast to exceed 100 in the valleys 
west of the Blue Ridge and 105 along the I-95 corridor. Humid 
conditions continue overnight, with near record high minimum 
temperatures possible. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...Decreasing heat & thunderstorm chances leading 
into Labor Day weekend. 

On Saturday, high pressure builds at the surface over the Great 
Lakes further advancing a cold front south across our region. Drier 
air trailing behind this boundary will stabilize conditions and 
reduce thunderstorm chances through the weekend. Brief showers or 
thunderstorms remain possible as a few disturbances round the base 
of the upper-level trough, but overall, no hazardous weather is 
expected through the beginning of next week. Through the long 
weekend, day time temperatures continue to drop back into seasonable 
conditions for early September. With dew-points in the low to mid 
60s, seasonable temperatures, and relatively low precipitation 
chances, Labor Day weekend is shaping up to be a pleasant September 
weekend.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Light winds and prevailing VFR conditions are expected across  
the terminals through Thursday. Showers and thunderstorms are
possible in NE Maryland this evening, so have a PROB30 for KMTN
and KBWI. For Wednesday and Thursday, daily shower and
thunderstorm chances yield periods of sub-VFR conditions.
Currently have a PROB30 for KIAD and KDCA for tomorrow evening 
for -TSRA. Convection will move into the TAF periods this
evening and will be added at surrounding terminals. 

Periods of sub-VFR conditions could persist Friday as showers and 
thunderstorms track across the area primarily in the afternoon & 
evening hours. Some of these storms could become severe. On Saturday 
afternoon and evening, terminals west of I-95 could experience sub-
VFR conditions as thunderstorm and shower chances return in the 
afternoon and evening. Westerly winds shift north to northeasterly on 
Saturday with gusts below 20 kts.

&&

.MARINE...
SMWs possible this evening across upper Chesapeake Bay.
Otherwise, light winds are expected over the waters through 
Thursday. Chances for strong to severe storms over the waters 
increases each day with SMWs possible. For Wednesday and 
Thursday, convection chances cover all waters.


On Friday and Saturday, winds below 15kts most of the time, but 
higher winds and waves could during afternoon and evening showers 
or thunderstorms. Westerly winds shift north to northeasterly on 
Saturday.

&&

.CLIMATE...
Given slightly cooler trends seen in the guidance for daytime
highs, record high maximum temperatures seem unlikely. However,
record high minimum temperatures are possible.
